issues.Description:
Owner asked for age, race/ethnicity, education and household size. grid/acs.py now pulls 118 E+M variables (every cell verified against the live 2023 variables.json; fetched in 3 chunks of ≤48 because the Census API caps a request at 50): median age (B01002); under-18, 18–34 and 65+ shares from B01001 summed across sexes, with 35–64 deliberately left as the residual so a fourth column cannot read as independent; white, Black and Asian non-Hispanic and Hispanic-any-race shares (B03002); bachelor's-or-higher share of 25+ (B15003); average household size (B25010) and one-person-household share (B11016). MOEs travel with every field: RSS for apportioned and multi-cell sums, the handbook proportion formula for shares, the incumbent weighted mean for the two intensive fields. A B01001-vs-B01003 per-tract population cross-check (>2% aggregate raises) joins the D54 B25044/B25003 one. Population-weighted hex figures against known NYC values: white NH 31.4% (~31), Black NH 20.7% (~22), Asian NH 14.6% (~15), Hispanic 28.5% (~29), college 39.7% (~40). Why the decision matters: these landed first on hex_demographics and were then COPIED onto address_gaps by containing hex — doubly modelled (tract→hex by unit share, hex→address by containment) and a step function at hex edges — while a parallel session built D56's tract-direct analysis.address_demographics the same day. Two tables answered one question. Ruling: the tract-direct table is canonical because a lot sits in exactly one tract and there is nothing to apportion; it was extended to the same 20 columns by IMPORTING acs.py's cell lists and helpers, the 36 hex-copied columns were stripped from the gap table, and a drift test fails if any hex demographic lacks an address twin. Unit-weighted citywide from the canonical table: white NH 35.0%, Black NH 19.1%, Asian NH 14.4%, Hispanic 26.7%, college 44.6%, median age 39.0, avg household 2.47 (units, not people, are the weight, so these differ from the hex figures by construction). Also caught: `loci address-demographics` had never been re-run after the extension landed, so every new column was NULL on all 767,337 rows until this session. Caveat the DB cannot enforce: share MOEs exceed 1 on a handful of near-empty denominators; gate on population before filtering on any *_moe. A catchment-weighted variant (demographics over the walk-shed rather than the lot's tract) is logged in QUESTIONS.md, not built.

Owner, on seeing 34 objects: "we need to really watch for proliferation of tables." Inventory showed the sprawl in the address layer — wide per-category tables that were pivots of an existing long table, a 200-row prototype (address_convenience) beside the table that replaced it, two orphans nothing wrote (address_gaps_prev, main.p), four hex screen outputs frozen since D38 (hex_gaps, hex_gaps_reach, hex_dnci, empty hex_outcomes), and two laundry-evidence tables with two views. Six items approved; five done, one rejected with reasons. Done: (1) one address-demographics source (D60); (2) orphans dropped; (3) hex screen outputs dropped, their writers and CLI commands retired under D38, the foundation hex tables kept because the address path still reads them for transit, jobs and reach; (4) `loci conveniences` is a read-only query over the long table — no second Dijkstra pass, nothing persisted; (5) the principled shape: analysis.address (one row per address: identity, summary, provenance stamped ONCE) + analysis.address_category (767,337 × 15 = 11,510,055 rows: nearest_m, ratio, and the D57 demand-annotation columns, which address_demand.py now writes by UPDATE only, with a pinned test asserting its SET-list is disjoint from the screen's own columns) and analysis.address_gaps as a VIEW generated from categories.yaml carrying every old column including the six provenance ones, so webmap_export, sql/004–006 and the supply-set tests work unchanged; (6a) address_laundry_evidence(bbl, source) replaces the two laundry tables and two views with one of each. Full suite 333 passed. issues.Title: Residential development pipeline: DCP Housing Database + DOB CO at job grain, pipeline exposure on analysis.address, webmap overlay
issues.Description:

Trap: 436 MN+BK jobs (11,407 units) are still marked Permitted in DCP but hold a CO issued after the cutoff; joined on job_number to override DCP status stale. Data problems: pkdm-hqz6 CO date is text (MM/DD/YY h:mm:ss AM), bs8b-p36w contains a literal 2105-11-05 (both handled in the adapter). One new table analysis.dev_pipeline (one row per DOB job, 48,762 MN+BK jobs at job grain), 12 measures extended analysis.address by UPDATE only (units_permitted_400m, units_completed_24mo_400m / _60mo_400m, nearest_large_project_id / _units / _stage / _date, pipeline_asof): reusing score/access network-distance helpers, NOT address_category (because exposure is category-independent). issues.Title: Storefront opening/closing history: inactive DCWP licences, full SLA history, DOHMH raw
issues.Description: Prerequisite for any lag or churn claim (QUESTIONS T7), and the reason the density-shock MVA could not run on 2026-09-09. The kill check that day showed Loci has NO storefront opening or closing time series: the only populated opened_on is Foursquare's record-creation date (a 17,453-row spike in 2010 is Foursquare's launch, not openings), the loaded SLA extract carries dates only from 2023-09, and no source has closed_on. Dating a present-day POI snapshot backwards would manufacture a clean event-time result under the null, because gentrifying areas lose more of their old openings (survivor truncation, Glaeser/Luca/Moszkowski 2023). So the series must come from records that include the dead: DCWP's inactive/expired licence file, the full historical SLA licence roster (originalissuedate on the ORIGINAL licensee, not a transferee), and DOHMH raw inspection history rather than the 3-year rolling window. Deliverable: opened_on/closed_on populated on staging.poi for those sources, with a per-source coverage-by-year table and an explicit statement of which years are complete. Not a new table. Gated behind the owner's call on whether T7's causal increments are worth building at all — the investor review found the rooftops→retail lag is a rational landlord option, not a friction. issues.Title: Stacked matched event study around ≥50-unit completions
issues.Description: QUESTIONS T7, increment 3 — the causal version, deliberately Low and gated. Given a building of N units receiving a CO at t (analysis.dev_pipeline, D62), what happens to storefront openings within 0–250 / 250–500 / 500–1,000 m over t−5…t+8 versus matched controls (same pre-period count, income, renter share, subway access, 2013–18 opening pre-trend, no ≥50-unit CO in the window)? Stagger-robust estimator (Callaway–Sant'Anna or Sun–Abraham), dose-response on log net units, SEs clustered at NTA with Moran's I on residuals. The flat pre-trend for τ ∈ [−5, −1] is THE falsification test; placebos are large non-residential COs (should move restaurants, not laundries) and randomised CO dates. Split treated buildings by PLUTO comarea > 0: if the whole effect lives in buildings with mandated ground-floor retail, the answer is supply, not demand. Why Low: this is D1 with the arrow reversed and inherits the development-cycle confound that sank D1; a hex-year panel also sits outside the address-level rule (D38). It exists as a ticket so the design is not re-derived; it should only be built if the owner wants the causal claim and the opening/closing history ticket has landed. Pushed to Linear 2026-09-10 as GTM-132.

issues.Title: Bar age-fit: market-revealed NYC age curve as a separate, non-filtering ranking signal (age_fit_bar, gap_score_fit)
issues.Description:
Owner, 2026-09-10, restating the request `docs/age_demand_fit.md` had refused: "a bar gap in the Upper East Side where avg age is 60+ vs a bar gap in the East Village where avg age is 25 — the East Village bar should score higher." The BLS CEX route stays rejected on its own numbers: alcohol spend is $643 per household nationally and $851 in the NY metro, but those are means over households *including non-drinkers*, alcohol is among the most under-reported lines in the survey, there is no age-by-metro table so the metro level and the age shape cannot be crossed, and the household shape peaks at reference-person 45–54 — the budget of a household, not the behaviour of a drinker; the owner's own gloss, "I spend $100 for 1 date", is exactly the distance between the two, and the resulting multiplier had a p10–p90 spread of 0.013 against a median MOE of 0.140 (dispersion 0.10) and scored the UES *above* the East Village. The replacement is measured on this warehouse: the median East Village address has 197 on-premises SLA licences, 55 bar-type licences and 87 canonical bar POIs within 400 m against Carnegie Hill's 49, 11 and 14 — 4.0×, 5.0× and 6.2× — so the market has already answered the question at 6× on the category-specific measures. Of the specifications `docs/bar_age_nyc.md` tested, exactly one was shipped: the COMPOSITION spec, outcome log(1+bar-type) − log(1+on-premises) within 400 m of the tract's residential centroid, on adult 18–34 and 65+ shares plus log units, log(1+CNS07 retail jobs), log walk-to-subway, log median income, renter share and borough FE, Conley 2 km spatial-HAC SEs over 1,065 MN+BK tracts; it reproduces at b(w18) = +0.404 (Conley se 0.203, t +1.99) and b(w65) = −0.484 (t −1.74), Carnegie Hill → East Village 1.298 [1.123, 1.500]. It was chosen because it is the ONLY specification whose two age coefficients both carry the owner's sign — every count specification has w65 *positive*, because the UES is old, rich and dense — and the only one significant in Brooklyn (b18 +0.596, b65 −0.662, t +2.44, ratio 1.451 [1.196, 1.761]), where 98.2% of the bar-lead gap set actually lives; the bar-POI count's Brooklyn CI grazes 1 at [1.011, 2.178] and Manhattan's composition effect is null at 1.124 [0.950, 1.331], so pooling alone would have calibrated where the signal is and shipped where it isn't. That criterion (F2) is now enforced in code rather than documented: `loci age-fit fit` recomputes the Brooklyn-only Conley CI and the dispersion gate and exits non-zero writing nothing if the CI includes 1.0 or the spread fails to clear its own median MOE — currently 3.61× (spread 0.200 against 0.055), a 36× improvement on the test that retired the predecessor. The caveat ships with the column and must render untruncated: it is SUPPLY-REVEALED (fitted on where bars already are, so demand and residential sorting are not separated), a low value is never evidence a neighbourhood does not want the service, and resident age is a proxy for a bundle — spatial-block CV says age adds +3.2–3.6% out of sample over a density-only model in Brooklyn but ≈0% once income, renter share, walk-to-subway and retail jobs are measured directly, and it transfers *negatively* (−1.1 to −1.7%) from Brooklyn to Manhattan. Stated honestly, the effect on the output: over the 67,223 bar-lead gap addresses in 82 clusters the multiplier runs p10/p50/p90 = 0.899/0.962/1.038, cluster Spearman 0.955 and address Spearman 0.983, and the top-50 cluster list changes by four clusters (Jaccard 0.923, two in and two out, max rank shift 20) — enough to answer the owner's question, little enough that gap_score still dominates, spread 1.66 against 0.20. Two data findings logged on the way: `analysis.hex_controls.subway_riders_2024` was NULL on all 8,321 rows for the plain reason that nothing ever wrote it — the column landed ahead of its loader and the registry entry was still `planned` — now fixed by `grid/mta.build_subway_ridership` chunking the ~110M-row hourly feed by calendar month because a whole-year server-side aggregation times out (8,321 hexes, 424 complexes; Staten Island correctly NULL, its nearest station being SIR); and `analysis.hex_panel` is not total LODES employment but exactly two NAICS sectors, CNS07 retail (303,835 jobs, 2023) and CNS18 accommodation-and-food-services (332,020), of which CNS18 must NEVER be a control for bars because food-service payroll *is* the outcome in employee form. Built: `age_fit`/`age_fit_moe`/`age_fit_source` on `analysis.address_category` (bar rows only; NULL, never 1.0, elsewhere — "no curve" is not "a neutral curve") and `age_fit_lead`/`age_fit_lead_moe`/`gap_score_fit` on `analysis.address`, all by UPDATE with both SET lists asserted disjoint from the screen's own columns before either statement runs; the generated `address_gaps` view exposes the three address-grain columns, appended; `loci age-fit fit` and `loci age-fit apply`, both with `--dry-run`; 20 tests in `tests/test_age_fit.py` (suite 364 → 384) covering the non-filtering proof (re-verified on the live DB: Σgap_score 938,319.24, Σn_missing 1,389,900, ratio>1 count 3,044,584 all unchanged), the disjointness pin, the NULL-vs-1.0 pin, the F2/F3 refusal-to-write and its non-zero exit code, and East Village 1.117 ± 0.090 > Carnegie Hill 0.834 ± 0.083 on the live curve.

issues.Title: Age-fit registry + childcare curve tested and REFUSED by the F2 gate (composition 0.767 [0.545, 1.078] in Brooklyn); bar unchanged
issues.Description:
Owner extended age_fit to childcare per QUESTIONS D15, on the reasoning that the supply-revealed placebo independently reproduced the CEX note's two passing categories with the same signs from a different source — the strongest available evidence that b(w18) is category-specific rather than generic urbanity — with the F2/F3 gate applied without relaxation, because two sources agreeing on a sign is corroboration and not a licence to skip the test. The spec mirrors bar deliberately: composition rather than count, `log(1 + canonical childcare POIs within 640 m) − log(1 + ALL canonical POIs within 640 m)` off the tract's residential centroid at the category's own reach tier, so that "this is a dense commercial strip" cancels out of numerator and denominator mechanically the way on-premises licences cancelled it for bar, with `under_18_share` as the primary demand regressor (children, not the age of adults) and bar's two adult shares retained so the placebo b(w18) stays comparable; controls, Conley 2 km SEs and the 1,065-tract MN+BK sample are identical to bar's. It failed. On 1,065 tracts (R² 0.551) b(under_18_share) is −0.205 pooled (Conley se 0.388, t −0.53) and −0.769 in Brooklyn (se 0.393, t −1.96), giving a Brooklyn contrast of 0.767 [0.545, 1.078] on East Village → Borough Park — the interval includes 1.0 and the point estimate is on the wrong side of it — while Manhattan runs the opposite way at +2.199 (t +2.98, ratio 2.586 [1.505, 4.446]), so the two boroughs are on opposite mechanisms even more sharply than bar; F3 passed comfortably at 1.49× (spread 0.117 against median MOE 0.078), which makes F2 the sole binding failure, exactly as the note predicted it would be. The contrast endpoints were derived from the panel rather than chosen — 79 MN+BK NTAs carry ≥500 addresses, and the extremes on unit-weighted under-18 share are East Village 0.069 (1,927 addresses) and Borough Park 0.464 (7,434) — and the count specification, fitted as a reported robustness check, is significantly wrong-signed at −1.862 in Brooklyn (t −4.52, ratio 0.542 [0.396, 0.741]), a CI that excludes 1.0 by rejecting the hypothesis rather than confirming it; F2 now tests the SIGN as well as the interval so that trap is closed in code, and nothing was switched. Two readings of the negative sign both forbid shipping: Borough Park's median address sits 375 m from the nearest canonical childcare against East Village's 205 m despite nine times the child share, which is either aggregator under-coverage of Hasidic home-based and yeshiva daycare — M1 wearing a costume, and childcare has NO registry anchor at all (`category_anchor` coverage 0.000; all 4,302 POIs are Overture plus Foursquare, so `in_principled` degrades to `in_all` and the outcome is built from the same supply the screen reads) — or a real desert, in which case the multiplier would rank the neighbourhoods with the most children DOWN, the D49/X6 hazard verbatim. Even had it passed it would have moved nothing: the 10,222 childcare-lead gap addresses sit in only 11 clusters, the multiplier runs p10/p50/p90 = 0.920/0.989/1.062 against a median MOE of 0.086, and cluster Spearman is 1.000. The under-5 robustness regressor, computed at tract level from B01001_003E + _027E in the raw ACS cache, enters at +0.783 and drives under_18_share more negative (Brooklyn −0.975, ratio 0.708 [0.513, 0.978]) — under-5s raise childcare composition, 5–17s lower it, net under-18 negative — so `under_5_share` and its MOE should be added to `analysis.address_demographics` in a future ACS pass, deliberately not in this one. Bar is untouched and proved so twice: the refit after the registry refactor reproduces every committed coefficient and the inputs hash `5b1374406fea` exactly, and applying both curves leaves all 281,839 bar rows bit-identical (digest `5bec24a6ed2c8d14`), with Σgap_score 938,319.24, Σn_missing 1,389,900 and 3,044,584 ratio>1 pairs unchanged; pharmacy remains open. Built: `CURVES`/`CategorySpec`/`ContrastSpec` in `model/age_fit.py` with radii read from `reach_tiers.yaml`, a k-term multiplier and delta-method MOE that raises rather than defaulting when a regressor has no ACS margin, per-category stale hashes and fit files, `loci age-fit fit|apply --category {bar,childcare,all}` with a reset pass scoped to what was requested so a gate-failed category is NULLed rather than left stale, and 12 new tests (suite 384 → 396, one deliberate skip: the childcare ordering test skips because no curve exists, so a future re-fit cannot ship without clearing it). Prerequisite to re-test childcare: load DOHMH child-care-centre inspections (dsg6-ifza) as the category's anchor.

issues.Description:

issues.Description:
Ruling 1 amends D52 rather than relaxing it: `childcare` now carries `anchor_is_floor: true` in `categories.yaml`, because D52's veto rests on the premise that a dense registry's silence is evidence, and for childcare that premise is false by construction — the DOHMH roster `gy3q-4tzp` covers Article 47 and Article 43 group settings only, while OCFS-licensed home-based Family and Group Family Day Care is published by no NYC feed, so the registry could not corroborate a home-based provider however real it is, and the veto was deleting supply precisely where home-based care dominates (`in_principled` had fallen 6,066 → 2,657 the moment the anchor qualified at coverage 0.846). The flag suspends only the lone-aggregator veto: the anchor still ranks first for canonical geometry and name, still feeds `anchor_coverage`, still qualifies, and `in_principled` for childcare returned to 6,066 — equal to `in_all` — moving citywide principled supply 138,403 → 141,812 and the live `supply_hash` f1b12ab55878 → 06bb6f357cc1; the flag is persisted on `analysis.category_anchor` and read by a new append-only migration `sql/013_floor_anchor.sql` so the view stays self-contained SQL, and it is folded into `supply_hash` so a rule change that moved nothing today still changes the stamp. Three tests pin the semantics — flag off, the veto still fires on the identical fixture; flag on, the lone aggregator is retained and `in_principled == in_all` for that category with the CORROBORATED ⊂ PRINCIPLED ⊂ ALL nesting intact — plus a drift check that refuses a floor flag on any category with no registry source measured in it, because a floor is a floor *under* a roster and flagging a category whose anchor was never ingested would be silently wrong the day one landed.

Ruling 2 splits F2 into F2a (the Brooklyn contrast CI excludes 1.0 with the stated sign, unchanged) and F2b (the primary demand regressor's own Brooklyn Conley CI excludes zero with that same sign), because F2a is a contrast over the whole age block and pharmacy cleared it in D66 at 1.585 [1.236, 2.032] while `b(age_65_plus_share)` carried a t of +0.90 — five-sixths of the contrast was "fewer 18–34s" — which is the GTM-109 defect, a number wearing a label it did not earn; the gate message now names which sub-test failed, a fit missing its Brooklyn SEs fails closed rather than skipping, and a fixture in which the contrast passes and the primary CI includes zero is refused by test. On the new supply, bar reproduces D63 exactly and passes (w18 +0.404 pooled, +0.596 Brooklyn t +2.44, contrast 1.451 [1.196, 1.761], dispersion 3.61×); childcare passes on materially stronger coefficients than D65's, `b(under_18_share)` +2.744 pooled (Conley se 0.446, t +6.15) and +2.302 in Brooklyn, East Village → Borough Park 2.990 [2.125, 4.208] pooled and 2.353 [1.662, 3.330] in Brooklyn, R² 0.601, dispersion 3.24× — different from D65's 3.556 because the floor anchor changed both the numerator and the all-POI denominator of the composition outcome; pharmacy is REFUSED at `b(age_65_plus_share)` +0.396, se 0.284, t +1.39, CI [−0.161, +0.954], and the D66 figure of +0.90 does not reproduce because it predates the anchor — the point estimate moves with the denominator, the verdict does not.

Ruling 3 applied both surviving curves and retired pharmacy's: its stale fit JSON was moved out of `data/interim` (a gate failure leaves yesterday's file in place by design, and `apply` then refuses on staleness rather than proceeding), pharmacy's 281,839 `age_fit` rows are NULL, childcare's 281,839 are populated with MOEs, and bar's 281,839 are unchanged in count. The screen was then re-run citywide in the canonical order — address-gaps ALL, address-demand ALL, pipeline, storefronts, age-fit apply — stamping supply_hash 06bb6f357cc1 on all 767,337 addresses; eligible rose 587,408 → 593,930 and Σn_missing 1,389,900 → 1,398,892, with the non-filtering identity exact on the new run (count{ratio>1, eligible} = 1,398,892 = Σn_missing), childcare-lead gaps falling 20,949 addresses in 45 clusters to 9,289 in 17, and bar-lead rising 144,731/230 to 148,221/240. The ranking barely moves: the top-50 MN+BK cluster list is identical by gap_score and gap_score_fit (Jaccard 1.000), bar-lead-only is 0.961 against D63's 0.923, and childcare's F4 ordering clears on the live curve with Borough Park at 2.306 ± 0.811 against East Village 0.718 ± 0.120 — passing, but with a band three times bar's, so childcare's multiplier must never render without its MOE. The UPDATE-only layers the rebuild cleared were re-applied and verified identical (pipeline 281,842/278,909; storefronts 281,842/281,835/9,625), `age_fit_lead` and `gap_score_fit` cover 267,327 addresses, the webmap was re-exported on the new gap set (142 files), and the D64 childcare live-ordering test that had been a deliberate skip now runs and passes: suite 503 passed, 1 skipped, that skip being pharmacy's live-ordering test, which is the state the ruling intends. The anchor is `keti-qx5t`, the NYS Medicaid Enrolled Provider Listing filtered to `profession_or_service='PHARMACY'`, defensible as a pharmacy roster in New York specifically because NYRx (2023-04-01) carved the pharmacy benefit for ALL Medicaid members into fee-for-service, so any pharmacy serving any Medicaid member must enrol and enrolment requires a current NYSED registration; weekly refresh, lat/lon published by the State on 100% of rows. Two silent bugs were caught by probing before building: `mmis_id` is per-PROVIDER not per-storefront (Ideal Care Pharmacy enrols 1621 and 811 Avenue U, 670 m apart), so the key is `mmis_id@address-slug`; and 8 rows carry a (0,0) null-island coordinate, dropped and counted rather than guessed. 2,416 records staged citywide (MN 448, BK 757, QN 719, BX 397, SI 95), hospital (1,270), clinic (142), specialty (11) and supervising-pharmacist (2,911) enrolments excluded by a closed vocabulary that raises on a sixth value and on a blank; `score/dedup.py` got the pharmacy branch (the D65 trap). `anchor_coverage` 0.000 → 0.903 against 1,330 MN+BK ZBP establishments, pharmacy qualifies; canonical pharmacy 5,536 → 7,105 `in_all` and 5,536 → 3,959 `in_principled` as D52's veto removed 3,146 lone-aggregator clusters (MN 534, BK 564, QN 599, BX 300, SI 94, 1,055 outside the res-9 grid); live `supply_hash` 06bb6f357cc1 → 767b28674e30, every other category bit-identical. `anchor_is_floor` deliberately left OFF: at 0.903 the file is above the "load a better anchor" band, the slice it misses skews affluent — the opposite of the bias that makes a veto dangerous — and unlike OCFS home-based care the true roster exists and is merely not downloadable. issues.Title: Manhattan listings coverage hand test: is 9% real or a search-query fault?
issues.Description:
The StreetEasy laundry sweep (≥6-unit stratum, completed 2026-09-11: 2,828 addresses, 4,813 credits) found advertised-laundry evidence for 47% of Brooklyn leads but only 9% of Manhattan leads (35 of 386). Building mix alone does not explain it: Manhattan coverage is low even in the 50+ unit tier, and listings.py's slug builder has a Manhattan-specific branch (the block that warns about reporting the Manhattan half of a sweep as zero coverage, a fabricated gap rather than a measured one).

Why it matters: the laundry demand haircut in the grade (D51/D55) will consume analysis.address_laundry_evidence (source='listing'). If Manhattan's 9% is a query fault, the haircut under-applies to Manhattan and every Manhattan laundry gap looks more real than it is. If it is genuine (Manhattan laundry leads skew to buildings with laundry rooms that never list amenities per unit, or to stock that never lists at all), it is a coverage fact to record and the Manhattan half must be treated as MISSING, never as absence.

Do: (1) take 12 Manhattan ≥6-unit laundry leads the sweep searched and found nothing for (no staging.listings row; a search call with the address in the fetch log's note), spread across neighborhoods and unit tiers; (2) rerun the sweep's search query exactly, then variants (no 'apartment', 'streeteasy' in the query instead of include_domains, house-number range forms, the slug-built building URL via Tavily extract), capped at 60 calls; (3) verdict per address: (a) listing exists and the query missed it = query fault, (b) building page says no amenity info = genuine silence, (c) nothing on StreetEasy = genuine absence; (4) if ≥3 of 12 are (a), fix the query/slug path with a test and estimate the Manhattan re-sweep (~386 addresses, ~700 credits); otherwise record in CHECKPOINT that Manhattan listings coverage is a measured 9% and the haircut uses the NYCHVS rate there.

Acceptance: a 12-row table (address, tier, sweep result, best variant result, verdict) and either a committed fix + re-sweep estimate or a recorded coverage caveat. Pushed to Linear 2026-09-13 as GTM-145.

issues.Title: Eligibility gate removed by owner ruling — every address in the universe; cap_m censoring flagged, not smoothed; citywide re-run on supply 767b28674e30
issues.Description:
The owner's words (2026-09-13): "I 100% vehemently disagree with 'which addresses count at all'. If an address is truly in a super underdeveloped area, this would completely not count it." The gate existed for exactly one reason — D39 found that the literal port, eligible iff within reach of ≥12 of 15 categories, violated monotonicity because tightening a reach dropped addresses out of eligibility faster than they gained gaps, and a FIXED, reach-independent presence test (≤800 m for ≥12/15) restored it — so retiring it needed a replacement for that role, and with no gate at all the role is filled trivially: the gap set is `ratio > 1` read off each address's own nearest_m against a reach that is fixed input, so tightening any reach can only ADD pairs, and the test now asserts reach × 0.8 removes exactly zero pairs over the whole universe rather than inside a mask. `eligible` survives as an always-TRUE column for schema and query compatibility (`WHERE eligible` in new code is now a bug, and the three surviving `eligible_only` parameters — sample, recommend, supply-ratio's baseline fit — are documented no-ops that exist only so a restored pre-D75 snapshot is not pooled with a gate-free one); `present_count` survives as the descriptive count it always was and is a candidate ranking feature, while the feasibility question the gate was reaching for stays where it belongs, in model/invest.py's PLUTO CommFAR/RetailArea build-or-lease test, with nothing folded across. D51's `cap_m` = 2,400 m censoring artifact, which the gate had been accidentally suppressing, is now fully exposed and is handled in the open by a flag and not a rule: `gap_score` and `cap_m` are both unchanged, because a censored ratio is still the smallest value that ratio could take and leaving it in keeps the ranking monotone, continuous and conservative, while `analysis.address_category.censored` and `analysis.address.lead_censored` carry the fact through the `address_gaps` view into the webmap's gap layer and popup, which now says "nearest X beyond 2,400 m — the distance was not measured" instead of printing the cap as a walk; 143,973 (address, category) pairs sit at the cap and 55,971 addresses have a censored LEAD (SI 20,864 / 18.6%, QN 17,511, BK 11,852, BX 5,734, MN 10), tailor_repair alone accounting for 111,512 of the pairs. The screen was then re-run citywide on supply 767b28674e30 — the second pass D71 deferred, and a genuine re-estimation because the pharmacy anchor moved every composition denominator: bar and childcare both clear their gates on the new denominator (bar w18 +0.404, Conley se 0.203, dispersion 3.61×; childcare under_18_share +2.762, se 0.447, dispersion 3.23×) and pharmacy is refused again on its own primary regressor at t +0.48, CI [−0.454, +0.749]. Over all 767,337 addresses the non-filtering identity is exact — count{ratio > 1} = 3,012,430 = Σ n_missing — against 1,398,892 on the gated D69 run; gap addresses rise 452,491 → 626,145, bar-lead gaps 130,892 → 180,480 in 240 → 264 clusters and childcare-lead gaps 1,342 → 1,775 in 17 → 18 (correcting D69's "childcare 9,289" the same way D71 corrected its bar figure: both counted eligible addresses whose lead was that category, non-gaps included). Every one of the 173,407 formerly-excluded addresses turns out to be a gap — none was a served address the gate had merely mislabelled — and they are overwhelmingly outer-borough: QN 74,050, SI 69,887, BX 14,957, BK 14,509, MN 4, leading on laundry 57,799, bar 49,613 and convenience 28,717, which is the shape the owner's objection predicted. The canonical order was re-applied in full and verified — pipeline 281,842 / 278,909 with units_active and units_stalled at 281,842, storefronts 281,842 / 281,835, age_fit_lead and gap_score_fit 281,840, homes_400m and supply_ratio 281,842 — and the MN+BK deliverable barely moves: the top-50 cluster list by capped units has member-address Jaccard 0.926 against D69, the same nine clusters lead in the same order, and the F4 orderings hold on the live curves (bar East Village 1.117 ± 0.090 over Carnegie Hill 0.834 ± 0.083; childcare Borough Park 2.316 ± 0.818 over East Village 0.716 ± 0.120, a band still seven times bar's). One consequence needed its own sanctioned exception: `supply_baseline.yaml` was fitted over the 267,329 addresses the gate admitted, so although the supply set itself did not move the baseline's universe did, and it was re-fit once on the gate-free universe (n 267,329 → 281,842, `universe` now recorded as "all addresses with homes_400m > 0", `supply_hash` 767b28674e30 unchanged, asof 2026-09-13) before the final `supply-ratio --boroughs MN,BK`, which raised no drift warning. The webmap was re-exported on the new gap set (145 files, 83.6 MB) with `meta.ageFit` listing bar and childcare on supply 767b28674e30 and `stale: []`, and the suite stands at 794 passed / 1 skipped, that skip still being pharmacy's live-ordering test. The owner also stated two further directions, recorded here and not yet built: sample an address near the middle of every known street in the borough so that undeveloped streets are represented, and rank by density.

Done 2026-09-13 (CHECKPOINT D75). Pushed to Linear 2026-09-13 as GTM-146.

issues.Title: Foot-traffic proxies: graduate transit/jobs from card context to a grade
issues.Description:
transit_entries_400m and jobs_400m shipped (commit 60d7b0b, CHECKPOINT D76): MTA hourly ridership entries and LODES WAC job-block centroids, walk-graph Dijkstra at 400 m network distance, on every MN+BK address. DOT pedestrian-count validation on 99 corridor points reads a headline ρ +0.79 for transit — strong enough to look grade-ready.

It is not. The contrarian red-team found the headline collapses under stratification: Brooklyn-only ρ is 0.56 with a CI floor of 0.14 — nowhere near the F2/F3 bar every other age-fit or demand column has had to clear (bar/childcare age-fit rulings, D63–D66, D69). 65% of Brooklyn addresses read a flat zero for transit, which is a coverage floor, not a measured absence. At the quiet end of the distribution, homes_400m out-predicts transit (+0.69 vs +0.62). And transit correlates +0.32 to +0.54 with supply_400m across every category — the endogeneity structure D1 exists to avoid.

For all of those reasons the columns must not enter a grade section and must not enter the supply_ratio_vs_base denominator (D73) until they clear a graduation test: (a) ≥100 non-corridor validation points; (b) Brooklyn-only ρ ≥ 0.6 with CI lower bound > 0.4; (c) a non-degenerate variable (800 m radius or distance-decay kernel) in place of the binary any-station-within-400m read. Until then the columns stay in recommend.py's context sections only, the same status age-fit had before D63.

Pushed to Linear 2026-09-13 as GTM-147.

issues.Title: Screen scope enforced, not defaulted: Manhattan + Brooklyn only — address-gaps refuses out-of-scope boroughs; out-of-scope rows pruned; re-run proves no per-address number changed
issues.Description:
The owner restated the scope in one line — "we are still focused on Manhattan and Brooklyn" — and the screen tables had quietly stopped obeying it: D61 ran `address-gaps --borough ALL` to attach the address-grain demographics, every re-run since matched that call out of habit, and `analysis.address` had been carrying all 767,337 addresses with `address_category` at 11.5 M rows ever since, so a reader of the deliverable was reading Queens and Staten Island alongside the two boroughs the project actually screens. A default was not enough, because a default is what D61 overrode: `SCREEN_BOROUGHS = ("MN", "BK")` now lives beside `BOROCODE` in `sources/cities/nyc/addresses.py` (the codes are NYC-specific, so `model/` and `score/` take the scope as an argument and still name no borough), `loci address-gaps` defaults to `MNBK` and REFUSES `--borough ALL` or any borough outside MN+BK before it opens the database, citing D48/D78, unless `--allow-out-of-scope` is passed for a deliberate documented run. Because `write_address_gaps` only delete-then-inserts the boroughs it is handed, a narrower re-run could never clean up after the wider one, so a new idempotent `prune_out_of_scope` removes out-of-scope rows from `address_category` and `address` together on every in-scope write; it took out 485,495 address and 7,282,425 category rows on its first pass and has returned zero ever since. The canonical order was then re-applied in full — address-gaps MN then BK, address-demand, pipeline, storefronts, age-fit apply (fits current on supply 767b28674e30, not re-fitted), supply-ratio, address-access, revenue, export-webmap — leaving `analysis.address` at 281,842 rows and `address_category` at 4,227,630, the non-filtering identity exact at count{ratio>1} = Σn_missing = 531,773 over 190,973 gap addresses, `lead_censored` at MN 10 / BK 11,852, bar-lead gaps 74,114 in 90 clusters and childcare-lead 52 in 1, and the UPDATE-only layers back at 281,842 / 278,909 / 281,835 / 281,840 with `access_run_at` NULL on nobody. The ruling changes the universe of rows and not one number inside it: Σgap_score is byte-identical at 412,007.8556131311, a 1,000-address sample matches the pre-run backup on all eight screen columns with zero differences, and the top-50 cluster list is identical by member addresses with no id relabelled. `analysis.address_demographics` deliberately stays citywide at 767,337 rows — it is the D48 data foundation, along with the raw sources, `poi_dedup`/`poi_supply` and the hex tables, because a POI in Queens is still the nearest pharmacy to an address in Brooklyn; `address_laundry_gaps` is a view and followed on its own. Layers keyed on `analysis.address` rows (the access columns, the transit profile) are rebuilt underneath by address-gaps and must be re-applied in the canonical order. Webmap re-exported (145 files, 83.6 MB) with `meta.ageFit.gapsSupplyHash` 767b28674e30 and `stale []`; suite 857 passed / 1 skipped.

issues.Title: Storefront filings: widen the lifecycle coverage beyond food/drink and harden the cross-agency link
issues.Description:
D80's analysis.storefront_pipeline (commits 2979cc2, 10a33e8; CHECKPOINT D80) proves the filing-chain approach works (fitout_filing → first_inspection strict median 259 d, N=67), but the coverage is structurally lopsided and the cross-agency link is thinner than the headline numbers suggest.

openings_pipeline_400m is structurally zero for 10 of the 15 categories — laundry, hair, nails, childcare, clinic, fitness, bank, hardware, convenience, tailor — not because nothing is opening in those trades, but because they are licensed by NYS DOS or NYS Education Department, or not licensed at all, and none of the DOB feeds carry a trade field that would let a filing be attributed to one of these categories. This must never be read as "nothing is coming" for those categories — it is a filing-blind spot, not a market signal. Candidate feeds: NYS DOS licensed professions, NYS OCFS childcare licenses, NYS/NYC DOH Article 28 clinics, DCWP laundry (already ingested but currently maps to no category — fix the mapping, don't re-ingest), and NYC DOB sign permits with tenant text as a fallback cross-check.

The cross-agency reconciliation links 2,613 pairs, but 92% are sole-pair-in-BBL, so the reconciled lead-time medians (e.g. 221 d N=741) are weaker evidence than the strict same-record medians (259 d N=67) even though the reconciled N is larger. DOB business_name on job filings is the building owner, not the tenant. SLA pending licenses are a live queue with no history — a skipped monthly snapshot is a permanent hole, same rule as the D79 first-seen ledger. One bug to fix in the next supply re-run: dohmh.classify("Steakhouse") currently maps to cafe_bakery; it should map to restaurant.

issues.Title: Site-revenue model v0: CEX spend pool × fitted capture share, leakage calibrated to Economic Census county receipts, gated by a leave-one-ZIP-out backtest — restaurant alone ships
issues.Description: Owner: 'can we try to predict what a business could make?' Anchors verified before building (Economic Census 2022 county × NAICS is the finest public revenue truth; CEX national spend by income quintile; NY-metro rebase; trade benchmarks not trusted without census check). Model: src/loci/model/revenue.py with Huff-model capture share (distance decay β and competition elasticity γ), fitted per leave-one-ZIP-out fold with sign free — the textbook negative sign was WRONG for 7 of 10 categories at ZIP grain (incumbents proxy 'is this a retail street?'), a result not a bug; leakage λ per county to match EC receipts (λ_Kings vs λ_NY disagree 1.4–2.6×, both carried). Gate: out-of-sample Spearman against CBP employees per establishment must beat county-baseline AND homes-only baseline AND cross-category placebo. Result on MN+BK 281,842 addresses after D75/D78: RESTAURANT alone passes — ρ_oos 0.763, R² 0.577, β 0.50, γ −0.25 (stable 65/73 folds), placebo pass; café/grocery/hair/nails/pharmacy beat baselines but fail placebo (commercial intensity); laundry/convenience/bar fail baselines; fitness too sparse. Grades modelled category C ('uncalibrated to local P&Ls'), never higher. Gowanus core restaurant revenue p25/p50/p75 $1.08M / $1.67M / $2.66M (1.81× Kings avg), rent ceiling $11.2k/mo. Caveats: county-level blur, national CEX, no edge-shed households, λ has no OOS test, backtest on establishment count only, parameter bands not outcome dispersion. 884 tests passed / 1 skipped / 1 concurrent rebuild lock failure.
